summary.headline: Punjab & Sind Bank Q1 FY27: business up 15.27% YoY to Rs 2,66,420 crore, advances up 19.35%, net profit up 23.05% to Rs 331 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported 19.35% YoY advances growth and 12.16% deposit growth, with NII up 15.33% YoY. Operating profit was flat at about Rs 545 crore despite lower treasury (Rs 80 crore vs about Rs 200 crore a year earlier) and lower written-off recoveries. Asset quality improved on a YoY basis (GNPA 2.21%, NNPA 0.65%), but the quarter included about Rs 123.5 crore of provisions, of which about Rs 150 crore was ECL build-up, which management said was proactive. Management kept FY27 guidance intact and said advances growth of 18-20% is achievable.

vs about Rs 200 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail advances grew about 36% YoY and make up 25.82% of the book. Retail term deposits grew about 14.94%.

segments.name: Agri
segments.commentary: Agri advances grew 25%+ YoY and make up 13.38% of the book. Food and agro processing is described as the bank's champion sub-segment.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME advances grew over 32% YoY and make up 20.82% of the book. Slippages were seen mainly in MSME accounts.

segments.name: RAM (Retail, Agri, MSME)
segments.commentary: RAM is 60.02% of advances, against a year-end target of 64-65%. The bank is pursuing this through branch activation, digital journeys and co-lending.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book is about Rs 4,000 crore. Co-lending share is about Rs 10,000 crore across gold loans, per the call; management expects about Rs 3,000 crore of net addition during the year.

guidance_outlook: Advances growth guidance of 16-18% for FY27 is maintained; management now sees 18-20% (and 19-20% possible) going forward.
Deposit growth guidance of 13-14% was missed slightly in Q1 and is maintained.
NIM target of 2.60-2.65% for FY27, versus 2.53% in Q1.
ROA target of 0.85-0.90%; ROE target of about 12%, versus 10.85% in Q1.
Cost to income to be below 60% in FY27, with an aspiration of below 50% in two to three years.
Credit cost guidance below 1%, including ECL build-up ahead of the 1 April 2027 ECL regime.
Core fee income target of Rs 900-1,000 crore for FY27.
Net slippage for FY27 to stay below Rs 677 crore (FY26 level), with a hope to bring it below Rs 600 crore.
Three-year plan: business of Rs 4,00,000 crore by FY29, 2,000 branches, about 1,600 ATMs and 6,000-6,500 business correspondents.
FCNR(B) and ECB/overseas borrowing mobilisation estimated at about USD 100 million; FCNR(B) alone estimated at USD 20-25 million. GIFT City branch expected around November.
qa_highlights
question
Why did the bank's QoQ business and advances growth look subdued in Q1 compared with peers?
answer
Management said Q1 is always subdued and the bank paces growth QoQ. It maintained 16-18% guidance, expects 18-20% going forward, and cited Rs 15,000 crore of undisbursed sanctions.
question
Why did net profit fall QoQ, and why did provisions rise?
answer

Management said additional provisions (Rs 123.5 crore vs Rs 20 crore in Q4) were proactive ECL build-up, not asset quality deterioration. It said about Rs 150 crore was ECL provision this quarter and that PCR rose to 92.33%.
question
Which FY27 ratios are being targeted?
answer
NIM 2.60-2.65% (Q1: 2.53%), ROA 0.85-0.90%, ROE about 12% (Q1: 10.85%), cost to income below 60%.
question
What is the net worth change, and what drove it?
answer
Net worth Rs 12,500 crore vs Rs 11,945 crore in Q4. The CFO said the AFS component was Rs 170 crore and the remainder was due to a DTA adjustment.
question
What is the FCNR(B) and overseas borrowing opportunity?
answer
Management estimates FCNR(B) at USD 20-25 million, with the total from all routes at about USD 100 million. Lack of a foreign branch and the GIFT City branch in about November limit the leveraging.
question
What is the gold loan trajectory and co-lending mix?
answer
Gold loan is about Rs 4,000 crore. Co-lending is about Rs 10,000 crore across gold loans, with about Rs 3,000 crore of expected net addition in the year. Agri gold loan is about Rs 419 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Which FY27 ratios are being targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: NIM 2.60-2.65% (Q1: 2.53%), ROA 0.85-0.90%, ROE about 12% (Q1: 10.85%), and cost to income below 60%, with an aspiration below 50% in two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net worth change, and what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: Net worth is Rs 12,500 crore vs Rs 11,945 crore in Q4. The CFO said the AFS component was Rs 170 crore and the remaining difference was due to a DTA adjustment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FCNR(B) and overseas borrowing opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: FCNR(B) is estimated at USD 20-25 million, with about USD 100 million from all routes including ECB and overseas borrowing. Lack of a foreign branch limits leverage; GIFT City branch is expected around November.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gold loan trajectory and co-lending mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Gold loan book is about Rs 4,000 crore, with co-lending about Rs 10,000 crore and expected net addition of about Rs 3,000 crore in the year. Agri gold loan is about Rs 419 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q1 provisioning is ECL vs normal NPA provisions, and is the credit cost guidance of below 1% realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 150 crore was ECL provision this quarter. Management said core credit cost should be very low as no red flags are seen, and the sub-1% guidance is a prudent buffer for ECL when it kicks in on 1 April 2027.

qa_highlights.question: How will NIM evolve given funding cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated FY27 NIM guidance of 2.60-2.65% versus 2.53% in Q1, citing higher-yield asset deployment and negotiation on pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Will MSME slippage stress continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the current run rate may continue given global trickle-down to MSMEs, but it is not alarming. FY27 net slippage is targeted below Rs 677 crore (FY26 level), with hope to go below Rs 600 crore.

capex_capacity: Three-year plan: business of Rs 4,00,000 crore by FY29, with 2,000 branches, about 1,600 ATMs and 6,000-6,500 business correspondents.
Presently in about 450 districts; branch expansion, recruitment and technology investment described as unavoidable cost drivers.
Zonal structure expanded from two to five zonal offices in Q1; back-office sanction (CENMARG) consolidated into five zones.
GIFT City branch expected around November (management said in one answer it would open in the third quarter); IT team working on it, approvals and team in place.
Digital gold loan and CBDC launch shortly; loan against mutual funds to launch digitally soon; further new initiatives likely after Q2.

Housing loan tie-ups with around 141 approved projects; car loan tie-ups with Maruti, Mahindra and Hyundai; STP limits raised to Rs 2 crore for home loans and Rs 50 lakh for commercial and pre-owned vehicles.
demand_pricing: Total business up 15.27% YoY to Rs 2,66,420 crore; advances up 19.35% YoY, deposits up 12.16% YoY; CASA up 10.2%; retail term deposits up about 14.94%.
Analyst noted QoQ growth of only about 1.25% in advances, 0.89% in deposits and 1.05% in business; management said Q1 is always subdued and the bank paces growth QoQ.
Segments: Retail up about 36% YoY (25.82% of book); Agri up 25%+ (13.38%); MSME up over 32% (20.82%); RAM at 60.02% of advances against a year-end target of 64-65%.
Undisbursed sanctions of about Rs 15,000 crore cited as pipeline support; management expects 19-20% credit growth to be possible.

Net interest income up 15.33% YoY; NIM 2.53% in Q1; management is replacing a low-yielding central government guaranteed exposure of about Rs 5,000 crore, with about 50% shed by 30 June and nearly all shed after.
Core fee income up 13.89% YoY; FY27 core fee target Rs 900-1,000 crore; collection efficiency about 95%.

Gold loan book about Rs 4,000 crore; co-lending in gold loans about Rs 10,000 crore; about Rs 3,000 crore net addition expected in the year; agri gold loan about Rs 419 crore; retail gold about Rs 5,600 crore.
Vehicle loans about 62% sourced digitally; home loans about 53% sold digitally; STP sanction rate about 40% in home loans and 50% in vehicle loans.
Treasury yield outlook: management said the domestic yield stands at 6.8% and could reach 6.90% shortly; global turmoil and crude near USD 90 make the outlook hard to call.
risks_watch: Treasury income volatility: Rs 80 crore in Q1 vs about Rs 200 crore a year earlier; management cited global turmoil, crude near USD 90 and yield movements.
ECL regime from 1 April 2027: build-up is ongoing and the sub-1% credit cost guidance depends on it.
MSME slippages and SMA levels; management targets SMA 1 and 2 below 3% of the book.
Deposit growth of 12.16% vs guidance of 13-14%, which was slightly missed in Q1; the funding cost pressure on NIM.
Recoveries from written-off accounts were lower in Q1 (about Rs 80 crore vs Rs 238 crore in Q4 per analyst), and management expects recovery to come mainly in the second half.
Shedding the central government guaranteed exposure of about Rs 5,000 crore at low yield; replacement pace affects NII.
Cost to income at 60.21% against a below-60% target; FCNR(B) and GIFT City timelines remain dependent on IT and approvals.
key_quotes: So overall business grew by 15.27% and stands at Rs 2,66,420 crores and it was spread between deposit growth of over 1 2.16% and advances of 19.35% .
We have undisbursed sanctions of around Rs.15,000 crores, we have done a lot of work on the digital asset side and our branch activation has improved.
So, the health of the cr edit portfolio continues to be r obust, and the capital adequacy now stands at a healthy level of 17.61%.
We thought it is better to fundamentally strengthen the balance sheet and that's why you will find that this time our PCR -provision coverage ratio also improved to 9 2.33%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the credit growth story and the FY27 guidance, which management says is broadly on track. Cautious on treasury income, which it called a market phenomenon that cannot be predicted, and evasive on the Q2 pipeline and the exact split of credit cost.
